Inside the prefix$ methods, its sanctioned members, computation is the type; DOM access and channel I/O keep their buckets and are judged against the host-bound shape

openQuestions.reason: same as React's utility modules; drift needs a declared shape

openQuestions.reason: the second review showed that a method defined on an unbound trait elsewhere excused the call, and that a one-line class formatted differently moved a score; both are gone. Single-file explain has no other files and trusts the spelling, and says so

The second review noted the two forms make an equivalent presence test; the policy is kept, with this qualification: the section admits no expression in that position, the JSX form admits any, and the tool counts evaluation in markup, not selection. A reader may prefer to count both as selection; the counts are in the JSON either way

openQuestions.call: a role's sanctioned members come from the Grammar: ViewStream carries only constructor, broadcastEvents, addActionListeners, onRendered (wiring-surface-only-on-viewstream); Channel constructor, onRegistered, addRegisteredActions, onViewStreamInfo (wire-in-onRegistered); SpyneTrait constructor and prefix$ methods (slice-traits-by-concern); DomElement its constructor. Members outside the surface are reported, not scored (2026-09-27)
openQuestions.reason: the same structural shape across every view is the claim; counting members against the card is how it is checked rather than asserted

openQuestions.call: string values in props.data, defaults destructured from props.data, and props.data.x = '…' inside a role class → V (2026-09-27)
openQuestions.reason: data handed to a rendering surface is the view's configuration: it declares what the template or component will be given, and is not copy in the wild. The same act gets the same bucket in both configs. Ruled 2026-09-22 as 'config = View, props.data included' and then lost when the seals came off; reapplied as a token rule. A hostile reader may say copy is copy; the answer is that copy inside markup is Content in both, and copy declared as data for markup is configuration in both

openQuestions.call: a string literal in JavaScript or TypeScript is not Content by itself: it takes its context (View in a view's configuration, Logic in a trait or a utility, Behavior in a handler). Content is a format: HTML and templates, JSX markup and its text, styles, JSON, Markdown (2026-09-27; JSON coverage implemented 2026-09-29, tooling manifests skipped)
openQuestions.reason: content is designated by where it lives, not by counting words. The second review noted what this cannot show: copy kept in a JS object reads as Logic in a React module and in a SpyneJS utility alike; moved to a JSON file it reads as Content. That is the position: copy belongs in data files and templates

openQuestions.call: console.* calls → L wherever they appear, arguments included, markup strings included (2026-09-27)
openQuestions.reason: console output is the developer's instrumentation, which is logic

openQuestions.call: a static class or className attribute value counts one Content token per class, in JSX and in an HTML template alike (2026-09-27)
openQuestions.reason: styles are a content format, and a stylesheet already counts by word: `.card { padding: 16px }` is three tokens. A utility class list does the same work in the markup and counted as one token however many classes it held, so a Tailwind codebase read smaller and less Content-heavy than it is, against a codebase that keeps its styles in SCSS files. A computed class list (clsx, cn) stays Logic with its arguments: choosing classes by state is a decision

openQuestions.call: inside a role's sanctioned members (ViewStream: constructor, broadcastEvents, addActionListeners, onRendered; Channel: constructor, onRegistered, addRegisteredActions, onViewStreamInfo; SpyneTrait: constructor and prefix$ methods) every token is the module's type: a default, a ternary, a trait call, a payload filter, a local call that feeds a property. Only a classifier marked `operation` keeps its bucket there: DOM access, channel I/O, a subscription, a fetch, console output, markup, styles, data configuration. A member outside the surface is out of place in full, whatever its tokens do (2026-09-29)
openQuestions.reason: a module that is VBL structure is its type, and anything inside it that is a property defining that type stays categorized as that type (Frank, 2026-09-29). Noise is significant logic where it is not expected: a large method of its own on a ViewStream, which belongs in a trait. A conditional in a configuration is not a reasonable definition of noise. This replaces the 26 September rulings that a computed value inside configuration is Logic and that a composed trait call is permitted Logic; the second review read every token by operation, and that reading was not adopted, because it measures composition rather than the noise the definition names. An explicit operation of another layer still shows in a ViewStream or a Channel: a DOM query in a channel, a fetch in a view. In a SpyneTrait it does not, see `functions`

openQuestions.call: inside a SpyneTrait an operation of its host's layer is Logic: `el$`, `appendView`, a DOM write in a view trait; `getChannel`, `subscribe`, a fetch, a data call in a channel trait; `sendInfoToChannel` in either. The other layer's operation stays foreign and is drift: a channel trait manipulating the DOM, a view trait subscribing to a stream or adding a listener. A trait bound to both hosts, or to none, absorbs both. Only a content format (a template, styles, a class list) is foreign in a trait; data the trait receives in a payload or assigns to `props.data`, literal or not, is its logic (review 3, 2026-09-29). The trait's expected shape is Logic alone; the host-bound shapes and the permitted transmit are retired (2026-09-29)
openQuestions.reason: the traits are the designed logic modules for the ViewStream or Channel instance: globally shared, removed from HTML, JSON, and style Content and from the ViewStream or Channel structural configuration. Saying that a ViewStream trait has views is noise, or a channel trait has behavior is noise, becomes absurd, because then what is the purpose of the trait in the first place (Frank, 2026-09-29). In the framework's own diagram the Logic circle overlaps View as Interactive Functions and Behavior as Data Driven Functions, and those overlaps are trait functions by design. Noise in a trait is a template, a stylesheet, JSON, or a view's configuration written into it, or a method outside its prefix$ surface. What makes a trait noisy is a channel using it to manipulate the DOM, or a view using it to add event listeners, run stream logic, or control what a channel does (Frank, 2026-09-29): a module of pure functions, testable as such and then applied to a `this`, is clean, and nothing in React is as enclosed. A trait is not holding content: an agent is not going into the trait to update templates, styles, or JSON. Part of a view's job is to sync its designed DOM content to the correct context, which means receiving content in the parameters of a method; ViewStream allows data as a string literal, and it is still data in JavaScript terms (Frank, 2026-09-29)

openQuestions.call: `sendInfoToChannel` and `disposeViewStream` take their host's bucket: View inside a ViewStream, Logic inside a trait, Behavior in a channel (2026-09-29)
openQuestions.reason: they are internal methods of ViewStream and expected there: the view sending its own info, or disposing itself, is the view's act, not a behavior layer reaching in. Reverses the 27 September reading that the transmit is Behavior permitted from a view trait

openQuestions.call: a ViewStream expects View and Content, not Behavior: its listener table, broadcast table, and `sendInfoToChannel` are View, and a `getChannel`, a `subscribe`, an `addEventListener`, a fetch inside it is out of place (2026-09-29)
openQuestions.reason: a view adding event listeners, running rxjs logic, or in some bizarre way controlling what a channel does is noise (Frank, 2026-09-29). Behavior had been in the expected set since 0.1.0 because a view transmits; with the transmit read as the view's own act there is no Behavior a view is expected to hold

openQuestions.call: `addEventListener` is Behavior, its handler body Behavior (2026-09-29)
openQuestions.reason: the framework's way is `broadcastEvents`; a manual listener in a view or a view trait is behavior wiring outside the channel system and shows as out of place

openQuestions.call: a `prefix$` call from a designated member is the host's own, whether the trait is bound through `props.traits` or used as a pure static function; a call to a method no trait in the codebase defines is named `:unverified` in the report but takes the member's type and is not drift (2026-09-29)
openQuestions.reason: the point of a trait is that it is a pure function, not that it is listed in props.traits; if the logic is in traits and the call is in one of the ViewStream's designated methods, it is not noise (Frank, 2026-09-29). Replaces the 29 September gating of trait calls by the host's bound traits, which review 3 showed was read from raw text: a binding inside a comment excused a call, an import alias failed, a same-named class elsewhere was accepted. Bindings are now read with the parser and reported on the trait, and they decide only which layer's operations the trait absorbs

openQuestions.call: the keyword that introduces markup (`return`, `const x =`) takes the bucket of what it introduces: View before a component, Content before host markup, in both configs (2026-09-29)
openQuestions.reason: an agent or a developer does not distinguish a return from what it returns: `return <Skeleton />` is a view, one concern; what makes a page View and Content is the host markup around the components it places (Frank, 2026-09-29)

openQuestions.call: a value handed as data takes the data rule whether or not it is formatted: a string in `props.data` or in an object-literal prop is configuration in a view and logic in a trait, tags or no tags (2026-09-29)
openQuestions.reason: data and HTML are both content, formatted or not formatted (Frank, 2026-09-29): the format of a value does not change what the value is to the module that holds it. Review 4 asked that recognizable markup inside a data value take precedence as Content; not adopted. Markup precedence applies to markup written as code, a template literal returned or assigned as a template, not to a value delivered as data

openQuestions.call: a `prefix$` call from a ViewStream, a Channel, or a trait its host inherits is resolved when any trait in the codebase defines the method, static or instance; only a method no trait or static function defines is named `:unverified`, on the bare form as well as the composed one (2026-09-29). Resolution covers trait methods, `$`-named exported functions, and `$`-named static methods anywhere in the codebase (review 5)
openQuestions.reason: calls to utilities simpler than traits are pure functions, logic, not missing; an agent or developer can see the import. Only a mysterious method that cannot be traced immediately to a static function or a trait method is unresolved (Frank, 2026-09-29). Review 4 found the bare form skipped the name; fixed

openQuestions.call: an import binds only the trait it names, through the file's export table (aliases included); an import that matches nothing binds nothing, and the trait then absorbs both layers as unbound; a reference with no import is a class in the same file, else a unique name (2026-09-29)
openQuestions.reason: review 5 showed an explicit import that matched no trait falling back to a same-named trait elsewhere: a unique name is not evidence when the import points somewhere else
